title: Customer activation blockers synthesis (Support/CS/Sales) — mapped to lifecycle nudges + emails
content:
Purpose
Synthesize the top qualitative activation blockers observed by Support, CS, and Sales for self-serve / PLG developers, and map each blocker to proposed interventions for the Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (emails, console nudges/checklist, docs/quickstarts, and sales-assist triggers).

Scope / how we gathered input
- Time window: last ~6 weeks of self-serve onboarding + recent “lapsed signup” outreach.
- Inputs:
  - Support ticket tags + notes (esp. auth, 4xx/5xx, streaming, console navigation).
  - CS onboarding calls (startup + mid-market) where first production-like request failed.
  - Sales inbound/prospect questions attributed to onboarding/retargeting messaging.
- Output intentionally avoids PII; examples are paraphrased.

Executive summary (what’s preventing first success)
Across Support/CS/Sales, the same three categories dominate:
1) Authentication & API key confusion (key creation, wrong env var, wrong project, permissions) → leads to immediate 401/403 and drop-off.
2) “First request” errors and unclear troubleshooting (bad curl/SDK snippet, headers, model name confusion) → leads to repeated retries without understanding what to change.
3) Streaming disconnects / websocket/SSE confusion (client/network handling) → leads to perceived unreliability and early churn, even when non-streaming works.
Secondary blockers:
- Model selection confusion (which model for chat vs embeddings, context length, cost/latency tradeoffs).
- Console navigation mismatches (docs/email links to outdated routes; users can’t find “where to run the first request” or “where to see latency/cost”).
- Billing/limits confusion (free credits vs quotas; sudden 429 / rate limits; how to increase limits).

Notable pattern: developers don’t distinguish between “platform bug” vs “integration mistake.” When the first error is not self-explanatory, they assume we’re flaky and stop.

Activation definition implication (for PM-412)
Support/CS sees meaningful “first success” in two tiers:
- Tier 1 (fastest): first 2xx completion from API (non-streaming OK) — strongest leading indicator that auth + basic request is wired.
- Tier 2 (production-like): first streaming success OR first dashboard view of latency/cost after a successful request — indicates they’re building an app, not just testing.
Recommendation: Use Tier 1 as primary activation metric for sprint (less confounded), and treat Tier 2 as high-intent milestone tracked as a secondary success metric.

Top blockers (ranked) with signals + proposed interventions

1) Auth/API key creation & usage confusion
What we hear
- “I created a key but I still get 401.”
- “Which header is it again? Is it Bearer or x-api-key?”
- “I copied the key but the console says invalid / permissions.”
- “I’m in the wrong project/workspace; key doesn’t match.”
Likely root causes
- Users skip key creation step, or create it but don’t propagate correctly to local env.
- Confusion between org/workspace/project scoping.
- Ambiguous error messages (401/403 without next steps).
Detection signals (instrumentation)
- api_key_created event without subsequent first_request_success in 30–60 min.
- first_request_error where http_status in [401,403] OR error_code indicates auth.
- Multiple failed requests (>=2) within 10 minutes with same auth error.
Proposed interventions
Console nudge/checklist
- Checklist step 1: “Create API key” (deep link to key creation screen).
- JIT banner when auth errors occur: “Auth error — check header + project + env var (2-min fix)” with a “View troubleshooting” link.
Email
- Email 1 (welcome): include a single canonical auth snippet (curl + SDK) and call out exact header format.
- “First-success rescue” email if api_key_created but no first_request_success after X hours (suggest X=6h initially): provide quick checklist + link to troubleshooting section.
Docs/quickstarts
- Ensure quickstart clearly shows where to paste key, and prints a friendly message on 401.
Sales/CS triggers
- If prospect repeatedly hits 403 (permissions) AND company domain is enterprise-ish (security/compliance questions), route to sales-assist (they may need org setup guidance).

2) First request fails (bad snippet, wrong endpoint, headers, JSON shape)
What we hear
- “The curl example returns 400; what am I doing wrong?”
- “SDK throws an error but I don’t know if it’s my network or the API.”
- “I’m not sure which endpoint to use for chat vs embeddings.”
Likely root causes
- Copy/paste drift between docs, emails, and console example.
- Users use older OpenAI-shaped payloads and assume compatibility.
- Missing required fields (model, messages vs input, etc.).
Detection signals
- first_request_error with http_status in [400,404] OR validation_error.
- High click-through to “docs” but no success event.
Proposed interventions
Console
- Inline “Copy curl” example on first-run page that is guaranteed to work (uses their project ID + model preselected).
- Error-aware nudge after 2 validation errors: “Looks like your payload shape is off. Here are the 2 most common fixes…”
Email
- Email 2 (quickstart): push a single “Hello inference” snippet (1 min) and link to “Common first-request errors (400/404)” section.
- Add a troubleshooting CTA that is framed as developer-first (“See exact fixes for 401/400/404”).
Docs/quickstarts
- Keep one canonical snippet (source of truth) that email/console both reference.
- Ensure examples for both Python + TypeScript are aligned.

3) Streaming disconnects / SSE handling issues
What we hear
- “Streaming works for a bit then stops / disconnects.”
- “How do I parse the chunks? I don’t see tokens.”
- “We’re behind a corporate proxy; streaming fails.”
Likely root causes
- Client not handling SSE properly (closing connection early, timeouts).
- Corporate proxy/load balancer buffering SSE.
- Users expect websocket semantics.
Detection signals
- first_streaming_start but no first_streaming_success within N seconds.
- streaming_error events (if emitted) or client-side “stream_end_reason=connection_closed.”
- Repeat retries with streaming enabled, followed by switching to non-streaming.
Proposed interventions
Console
- Checklist step: “Enable streaming (optional)” placed after “First request success.”
- JIT nudge when streaming fails: “Try non-streaming first, then enable streaming (here’s the known-good sample).”
Email
- Email 3 (next step): “Add streaming in 5 minutes” with a clear warning box: “If you’re behind a proxy, start with non-streaming; here’s the workaround.”
Docs/quickstarts
- Provide a streaming example + a short “If streaming disconnects…” checklist (timeouts, proxy buffering, keep-alives).
Support
- Add a canned response linking to streaming troubleshooting section; include “how to provide repro info” (SDK version, language, network/proxy, request ID).

4) Model selection confusion (chat vs instruct vs embeddings; cost/latency)
What we hear
- “Which model should I start with?”
- “I picked a model and got errors; is it not supported?”
- “We do embeddings; why do your examples focus on chat?”
Likely root causes
- Too many choices at first run; unclear defaults.
- Users can’t map their job-to-be-done to model family.
Detection signals
- Model changed multiple times before first success.
- High “model catalog view” without first_request_success.
- Embeddings users clicking chat quickstart.
Proposed interventions
Console
- Default model preselected by use case choice (“Chat”, “Embeddings”, “Rerank”).
- Nudge: “Not sure which model? Start with Redwood Recommended (balanced)” with short rationale.
Email
- Segment email CTA by declared intent (if captured) or by first endpoint visited.
- Add a lightweight “model picker” section: 3 bullets by use case.
Sales/CS
- If they ask about private/VPC early, avoid over-rotating on model catalog; focus on deployment + reliability and route them to appropriate PM/SE.

5) Console navigation + broken links / outdated routing
What we hear
- “Email link 404s.”
- “I can’t find where to run the request.”
- “Where do I see latency and cost?”
Evidence
- Support ticket about email links leading to wrong console path/404 after routing change.
Proposed interventions
- Audit all email + retargeting + docs links for canonical console paths before launch.
- Add a “Console paths redirect” safety net for known old routes.
- In-email CTA buttons should go to stable pages (project home, API keys, quickstart, usage dashboard).

6) Billing, credits, rate limits (429) & quota confusion
What we hear
- “I’m getting rate limited; did I do something wrong?”
- “Do I need a card to test?”
- “How do I raise limits?”
Likely root causes
- Credits/quota not visible early.
- 429 message not actionable.
Proposed interventions
Console
- Post-first-success nudge: “See your token usage + limits” (deep link to usage dashboard).
- JIT banner on 429: “You hit a limit — here’s how to fix: wait, lower concurrency, or add billing for higher limits.”
Email
- Include “what’s included in free credits” and “what triggers billing” in a short FAQ section.
Sales assist
- If user adds billing OR hits sustained limits quickly, flag as high-intent for sales outreach.

Mapping: blockers → sprint levers (emails vs console nudges vs retargeting)

A) Onboarding emails (welcome → first success → troubleshooting → next step)
- Email should prioritize: (1) auth snippet, (2) one known-good request, (3) troubleshooting for common errors.
- “Next step” should be streaming + dashboard viewing (latency/cost) only after first success.
- Triggering suggestions:
  - If signup but no api_key_created in 1h: send “Create your key (2 minutes)” email.
  - If api_key_created but no first_request_success in 6h: send “Get your first 2xx” troubleshooting email.
  - If first_request_success but no dashboard_viewed in 24h: send “See latency/cost + set a route” email.

B) In-console nudges/checklist
Checklist ordering (recommended)
1. Create API key
2. Make first request (copy curl / SDK)
3. Turn on streaming (optional)
4. View latency & cost dashboard
5. (Optional) Create a route / deployment config
Banner/JIT nudge rules (recommended v1)
- After 2 auth errors → show auth help banner.
- After 2 validation errors (400/404) → show payload help banner.
- After streaming failure → show streaming fallback guidance.

C) Retargeting (non-activated and lapsed)
Messaging tie-in to blockers
- If user never activated: ads/LP should emphasize “first request in 5 minutes” + “copy/paste quickstart” + “clear troubleshooting.”
- If lapsed after trying streaming: ads/LP should emphasize reliability + “streaming examples + known proxy workarounds.”
- Avoid overly broad “best latency” claims unless we can link to a benchmark page; keep it developer-specific: “predictable latency, easy debugging, clear cost visibility.”

Suggested event taxonomy additions / property notes (for ENG-2841 / analytics)
High value properties to attach to first_request_error / first_request_success
- sdk_language (python/typescript/none)
- request_type (chat/embeddings/rerank)
- is_streaming (true/false)
- http_status
- error_code (normalized)
- model
- region
- console_or_api_origin (console_try_it vs external)
- utm_campaign/utm_source when present

Customer verbatims (paraphrased)
- “I’m blocked on the first step — I don’t know where to put the key.”
- “I assumed you were OpenAI-compatible; my payload didn’t work and I couldn’t tell why.”
- “Streaming looked great… then it just stopped. That felt risky for prod.”
- “There are a lot of models. I just want the recommended default.”

Open questions / decisions needed
- What is the exact primary activation event for sprint dashboards (first 2xx completion vs streaming success)? (PM-412)
- Should we gate streaming guidance until first non-streaming success to reduce perceived flakiness?
- Do we have a single canonical snippet “source of truth” that email + console embed (to prevent drift)? If not, decide owner.
- Where should we put the model picker: first-run page or model catalog (to avoid extra click)?

Immediate action items (week 0)
- Ben/Tyler: ensure email sequence includes a clear “auth + first request + troubleshooting” spine; confirm triggers/suppressions with privacy constraints.
- Marissa/Paula: confirm console checklist step order + nudge triggers; confirm instrumentation for error-based nudges.
- Dev/Support: add/update canned responses for auth + streaming; align links to the new troubleshooting page.
- Engineering: implement/verify event emission + normalized error codes; ensure broken console routes have redirects.

Appendix: quick severity rubric used here
- Severity 1: blocks first_request_success (hard stop).
- Severity 2: first_request_success possible but prevents production-like usage (streaming, routing, dashboards).
- Severity 3: confusion/friction but user can proceed without support.
